title: Sidebar: Prevent updating non-existent stories
body:
Closes #32997

<!-- If your PR is related to an issue, provide the number(s) above; if it resolves multiple issues, be sure to break them up (e.g. "closes #1000, closes #1001"). -->

Storybook maintainers cherry-pick bug and documentation fixes into the `main` branch as part of the release process, so you shouldn't need to worry about this. ## What I did

After identifying that the error was caused by `LeafNode` becoming `undefined`, I added logs in `code/core/src/manager/components/sidebar/Tree.tsx`.

The logs show:

```
Initial data prop: {..., example-button--primary: {parameters: {…}, ..., prepared: true}}
Item passed to Node: {parameters: {…}, ..., prepared: true}
```

These logs indicate that incomplete data was passed to the `Node` component — the `item` object was missing its `type` property.
As a result, `const LeafNode = ...[item.type]` evaluated to `undefined`, causing the render error.

Root Cause
The `updateStory` function incorrectly created an incomplete entry in the index when handling an update event for a story that had been filtered out.

Fix
Added an existence check in `updateStory` so it only updates entries that already exist.

## Testing

### Manual testing
_(added by @Sidnioulz)_

1. Open Storybook and select a story you know how to filter
2. Apply a filter to exclude the current story
3. Open DevTools or resize window to force a switch to the mobile layout
4. Attempt to open the sidebar menu button

Without the PR, I confirm a React crash occurs. With the PR, the sidebar opens (which incidentally clears filters due to https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/issues/32997 which I'm working on).

**Add defensive existence checks to updateDocs ref branch for consistency.**

The updateStory fix correctly adds existence checks in the ref branch. However, updateDocs's ref branch (lines 664-669) unconditionally updates `index[docsId]` and `filteredIndex[docsId]` without verifying those entries exist, mirroring updateStory's pre-fix vulnerability. Apply the same defensive pattern:

```
} else {
  const { id: refId, index, filteredIndex }: any = ref;
  if (index && index[docsId]) {
    index[docsId] = { ...index[docsId], ...update } as API_DocsEntry;
  }
  if (filteredIndex && filteredIndex[docsId]) {
    filteredIndex[docsId] = { ...filteredIndex[docsId], ...update } as API_DocsEntry;
  }
  await fullAPI.updateRef(refId, { index, filteredIndex });
}
```
